label: Claude Sonnet 5.5
output:
@Kavya, this is for you, and for everyone who has been tagging me since yesterday.

First, what I got wrong. When the first candidate applied, I knew where he was working. I should have called you before making the offer, not after. I treated it like any other hire, but between friends in the same cohort it isn't. That's on me, and I'm sorry. I understand why it looked bad from where you stood.

Now the facts, because a wrong number is going around and I'd rather it stopped here:

• We put up a backend dev opening on our LinkedIn page and Instahyre on 14 Sept, open to anyone.
• The first person applied on his own on 19 Sept. The second came about two weeks later, as a referral from the first.
• Nobody from my side DMed anyone.
• Both offers were 22% over their current CTC. Not 40%.
• On ESOPs: we do have a pool. It's small, but it's real and has been on paper since January.

Both joined us on 3 Nov. I won't name them. They didn't ask to be part of this and they shouldn't have to be.

Kavya, you sat with me in the Koramangala office till 1am fixing our Razorpay webhook mess before demo day. I have not forgotten that, and one bad week won't change it. You've helped me more than I can list in a post. I did message you after the second offer was accepted, but that was already too late. The call should have come first.

I'm not writing this to fight with you. I'm writing it because I respect you, and because staying quiet while the 40% number kept travelling didn't feel right either.

There's a bigger thing here. Foundry91 cohort 4 has 11 startups, and we're all hiring from the same small pool in HSR and Koramangala. This will happen again, to me, to you, to anyone in the batch. So here's a simple rule I'd like us to try: if you're interviewing someone who works at another company in our cohort, give that founder a heads up before the offer goes out. Not permission, just a heads up. It costs nothing and it keeps the friendships intact. Five minutes on a call would have saved all of us this week.

Kavya, coffee or a call is open this week, whenever you're okay. Happy to come to wherever is easy for you.

Would love to hear what the rest of the batch thinks about the rule.

---

It's about 417 words and roughly 2,450 characters with spaces, so it's within both limits.

- Type "@Kavya" fresh in LinkedIn so it becomes a real tag.
- I left out the blue tick. Mentioning it publicly would read as a dig. The line about messaging her after the second offer covers it without pointing at her.
- I didn't mention SitterNest or DabbaDost, since the post is about the cohort and the hiring, not the products. Easy to add if you want them in.
